Section 1 · Overview

The CXO Intel Loader is the single, gate-keeping entry point that converts a HoldCo's CXO bench into structured tenant data inside AbarVa. No Move ships against a HoldCo until at least the Wave 1 bundles (CIO + CFO) are loaded, validated, and acknowledged by the responsible CXO. The loader is the substrate proof point for the five locked rules in README.md: no claim without provenance, foundation-before-AI, no fake completion, HoldCo data sovereignty, and no demo-only data.

Where the loader lives in the UI

The loader is a sub-route of the Setup / Admin module. The route shape is:

RouteWho reaches itPurpose
/setup/cxo-intelHoldCo admin · HoldCo CXO · L0 admin (read-only across all HoldCos in group)Bundle index · per-bundle status · load history · approval queue
/setup/cxo-intel/[bundle]SameOne of: cio · cfo · coo · chro · gc
/setup/cxo-intel/[bundle]/uploadSameThe 6-step loader UX flow (intro → template → upload → preview → validate → approve)
/setup/cxo-intel/[bundle]/historySamePast loads · who ran · what was approved · diff vs current
/setup/cxo-intel/loads/[upload_id]SameSpecific load event · all rows · validation results · approval status

The loader is reachable from the Setup home page's onboarding card ("Load CXO Intel — 0 of 5 bundles loaded for Morgan Street"). It is also reachable from the Tower Federated tab's L0 view ("Morgan Street is at 2 of 5 bundles — review onboarding").

How the loader scopes data

Every loaded row is scoped to one HoldCo's tenant under that HoldCo's holding_group_id. The substrate enforces this via RLS on cxo_intel_* tables (see §9). L0 sponsor visibility is aggregate-only by default; transaction-grain access to a sibling HoldCo's data requires explicit grant from that HoldCo's admin (per the locked rule HoldCo data sovereignty in README §3).

The loader infers HoldCo scope from the active tenant context. The acting user must hold one of: tenant_admin, cxo_role:cio|cfo|coo|chro|gc, or data_steward. L0 users acting on behalf of a HoldCo must impersonate via the documented L0 ops shim (/admin/tenant/impersonate), with full audit trail.

How the loader fits into Wave 1 sequencing

Spec L02 (Wave 1) ships CIO + CFO loaders. Spec L08 (Wave 2) ships COO + CHRO + GC. The Wave 1 / Wave 2 split is driven by Move dependency: Move 0 (Kyriba de-risk) needs the CFO bundle; Move 1 (AI on top of Kyriba) needs CFO + CIO; Move 2 (cross-HoldCo cost reduction) needs CIO + CFO + GC across at least 2 HoldCos. Move 3 (federated IT) needs CIO; Move 4 (federated risk) needs CHRO + GC. By shipping Wave 1 first, Moves 0, 1, and Move 2 partial all become reachable.

Section 2 · Common loader UX pattern

Every CXO bundle uses the same six-step UX flow. Codex implements it once as <LoaderFlow bundle={...} schema={...} /> and the per-bundle pages plug in their schema descriptor. This keeps the UX legible, audit-traceable, and reusable across all five bundles plus future bundle types (e.g., CISO bundle in Wave 3).

Step 2 · Template download

The loader hosts canonical CSV templates per bundle file. Each template has:

  • Exact column headers in the documented order
  • One example row drawn from Morgan Street's fictional seed (so the CXO sees a plausible filled-in row)
  • An instructions row as the second row, prefixed with #, that explains required vs optional + validation rule per column
  • A footer link to this spec for the full schema documentation

The example row is generated server-side from the Morgan Street seed when the user is in Morgan Street tenant context; from Roosevelt seed when in Roosevelt; etc. This makes the template self-teaching.

Step 3 · Upload & parse

Drag-and-drop area accepts multi-file selection (the bundle's full file set in one go) or per-file uploads (incremental fill-in over multiple sessions). Client-side parsing uses papaparse (already in repo) with header-row detection, type coercion deferred to validation step. The parser auto-detects encoding (UTF-8 default, falls back to Windows-1252 if CSV came from Excel on Windows).

If a file's headers don't match the expected schema headers, the loader surfaces a "header mismatch" preview with a per-column mapping dialog (user maps "Vendor Name" → vendor_name, etc.). The mapping is saved per-user-per-bundle so subsequent loads auto-apply.

Step 4 · Validate & preview

Each row is validated against the schema's validation rules (see §8 for the common rule set; per-bundle specifics in §3–§7). Three outcomes per row:

Red · blocks A required column is missing, a controlled-vocabulary value is invalid (e.g., currency code USDD), a foreign-key reference fails (e.g., bank reference doesn't match any row in the banking_relationships file), or a sanity-check fails so badly the row would corrupt downstream Moves (e.g., contract renewal date 50 years from now). Row is rejected from the load until fixed. User can edit inline and re-validate.
Amber · review Row passes structural validation but a soft rule fires (e.g., contract renewal date in the past, vendor name has no fuzzy match against the global vendor index, annual cost is outside the 99th-percentile band for its category). Row lands in the substrate with a flag for human review. CXO acknowledges amber rows individually or in bulk during step 5.
Green · clean Row passes all validation. Lands in the substrate with status validated.

The validation step is interactive: the user can fix red rows in place, paste corrected data, or drop the row entirely. Amber rows can be downgraded to green by the user attesting "I confirm this is correct" with an optional note.

Step 5 · Human ack + approval

The CXO (or delegated steward) sees a per-file summary plus a global summary across the bundle. Approval is a single explicit affirmative action with attribution. Approvals are immutable; subsequent re-approvals create new load events with diff.

I am authorized to load this bundle. | | | | Approver name: Sarah Lindqvist | | Approver role: CFO | | Approval method: [x] CXO direct [ ] Delegate on file (steward) | | | | Banking rows require co-approval from Group Treasurer: Aisha Vargas | | Co-approval status: [ Request co-approval ] | | | | [ Back ] [ Approve and load ] | +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Approval routing per bundle is documented in each section below (§3–§7). For the CFO bundle, the banking-relationships file additionally routes to the Group Treasurer for co-approval — this is enforced server-side, not just UI-side. The substrate write does not happen until both signatures are in.

Step 6 · Land in substrate

On approval, the loader runs a single transactional write:

  1. Create one cxo_intel_upload record (the upload event) — captures user, role, tenant, holding_group_id, bundle, files, approver, co-approver if any, ack timestamp, source IP, integrity hash of uploaded files.
  2. Insert all green + acknowledged-amber rows into the bundle's substrate tables (e.g., cxo_intel_banking_relationships, cxo_intel_app_inventory). Each row has FK upload_id linking back to the upload event.
  3. Mark the bundle's loader status as loaded · version N in the per-tenant bundle ledger.
  4. Emit a domain event (cxo_intel.bundle.loaded) so downstream Moves can recompute readiness.

On failure mid-write, the transaction rolls back; the user sees the failure reason and can re-approve once fixed. Partial bundles (e.g., 4 of 7 CFO files loaded) are valid intermediate states; Moves that depend on the missing file remain blocked with explicit messaging.

Attribution + audit trail

Every loaded row carries:

  • upload_id — FK to the upload event
  • loaded_by — user ID of person who hit upload
  • approved_by — user ID of CXO (or delegate) who approved
  • approved_at — timestamp
  • validation_status — green, amber_acknowledged, with optional amber_note
  • source_file — original filename (preserved for audit)
  • source_row_num — original CSV row number (for traceback)

This is what powers the "no claim without provenance" rule downstream: every sentence Sentinel generates that references a vendor, contract, bank, or comp data point can trace back to a specific loaded row, a specific upload event, a specific CXO approval. Sentinel's evidence chain links resolve via these IDs.

Section 3 · CIO bundle Wave 1

Purpose. Capture the HoldCo's IT estate end-to-end: the applications running the business, the cloud footprint, major vendor contracts, AI maturity + roadmap, IT spend allocation, the risk register, and the IT organization. This bundle is the source of truth for every downstream claim about a HoldCo's technology posture.

Moves that depend on it. Move 1 (architecture decisions about the lakehouse target reference cloud footprint + data plane state), Move 2 (vendor consolidation needs the app inventory + contract catalog), Move 3 (federated IT strategy + AI marketplace needs the AI roadmap + cloud posture), Move 4 (federated risk needs the risk register + IT org).

Owner. HoldCo CIO. For Morgan Street that is Daniel Okonkwo. Data steward is the IT PMO lead. CISO (Lena Hoffman at Morgan Street) is a co-approver on the cyber-relevant rows inside the risk register file.

CIO bundle · validation rules summary

  • FK integrity. vendor_contracts.linked_app_names must resolve against app_inventory.app_name within this load. Unresolved → red.
  • Sum-to-100 invariants. cloud_footprint.share_pct and it_spend_allocation.share_pct must sum to 100 ± 2pp.
  • Spend reconciliation. Sum of annual_value_usd in vendor_contracts should not exceed it_spend_allocation total (amber if it does — likely double-counting or untracked spend).
  • Cyber routing. Risk-register rows with cyber_relevant = true route to CISO co-approval.
  • Stale data. risk_register.last_reviewed_date older than 6 months → amber.

CIO bundle · failure mode (partial upload)

The CIO bundle permits partial loads — e.g., CIO uploads app_inventory + cloud_footprint + vendor_contracts but defers ai_roadmap + risk_register + it_org + it_spend_allocation pending data collection. Each missing file is tracked at the per-tenant ledger:

  • Move 2 (cross-HoldCo vendor) — needs vendor_contracts; works partial as long as that file is present.
  • Move 3 (federated IT) — needs ai_roadmap + cloud_footprint + it_org; blocked until all three present.
  • Move 4 (federated risk) — needs risk_register; blocked until present.

The Setup home shows: "CIO bundle 3 of 7 files loaded. Move 3 blocked pending ai_roadmap.csv, it_org.csv. Move 4 blocked pending risk_register.csv."

Section 4 · CFO bundle Wave 1

Purpose. Capture the HoldCo's finance posture end-to-end: finance system inventory (ERP/treasury/EPM/AP/AR), banking relationships, audit + advisory firm engagements, insurance program, close-cycle metrics, IT spend ratios, tax engagements. This is the load-bearing bundle for Move 0 (Kyriba de-risk) and Move 1 (AI on top of Kyriba).

Moves that depend on it. Move 0 (the entire 6-gate de-risk diagnosis), Move 1 (capability portfolio + business case), Move 2 (vendor consolidation joins on audit + insurance), Move 4 (federated risk + concentration).

Owner. HoldCo CFO. For Morgan Street that is Sarah Lindqvist. Data steward is the Controller. Banking rows additionally route to Group Treasurer (Aisha Vargas at Morgan Street) for co-approval.

CFO bundle · validation rules summary

  • Banking H2H ratio — drives Move 0 G1 risk grade. Must be present.
  • Close variance — close_cycle_metrics.gl_cash_variance_pct trailing-6-month avg drives Move 0 G2 grade.
  • IC posting cycle — close_cycle_metrics.ic_posting_days trailing-6-month avg drives Move 0 G6 grade.
  • IT spend reconciliation — it_spend_ratios.total_it_spend_usd must match (±15%) CIO bundle it_spend_allocation.annual_usd sum.
  • Auditor cross-HoldCo — fires Move 4 concentration once 2+ HoldCos load same firm_name.
  • Insurance carrier cross-HoldCo — fires Move 4 concentration once 2+ HoldCos load same carrier for cyber line.
  • Tax-audit independence — amber where firm_name in tax_engagements matches firm in audit_advisory_engagements (regulatory flag).

CFO bundle · failure mode (partial upload)

  • Move 0 unblocks when finance_system_inventory + banking_relationships + close_cycle_metrics are all loaded. Three of seven files is enough to begin Move 0 diagnosis.
  • Move 1 entry waits on Move 0 minimum (G1-G4 green or in-flight).
  • Move 2 vendor consolidation joins on audit_advisory_engagements; without it the audit-concentration thesis cannot fire (other vendor consolidation opportunities still proceed from the CIO bundle).
  • Move 4 concentration thesis fires partial; without insurance_program the carrier-concentration check is deferred.

Section 8 · Common validation patterns

Every bundle uses the same primitive validators. Codex implements them once in src/lib/cxo-intel/validators/* and the per-bundle schemas reference them by name.

Currency codes (ISO 4217)

Accepted: any 3-letter uppercase code present in the ISO 4217 active list (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF, CNY, INR, MXN, BRL, ZAR, plus all other active codes — checked against a static reference table in src/lib/cxo-intel/reference/iso4217.json). Rejected: lowercase, 4-letter, retired codes (e.g., DEM). Red on rejection. Implementation: the validator coerces to uppercase before checking; case-mismatch alone is auto-corrected with a comment, not blocked.

Dates (ISO 8601)

Accepted: YYYY-MM-DD only. Auto-coerce: YYYY-M-D, YYYY/MM/DD, MM/DD/YYYY (US-style) with a "best-guess" amber flag. Rejected: ambiguous formats (e.g., 02/03/2026 where it could be Feb 3 or Mar 2 depending on locale — red; user clarifies). Future-date sanity: more than 30 years out is red; more than 10 years out is amber. Past-date sanity: depends on column semantics — for "renewal_date", past is amber (likely stale or auto-renewed); for "engagement_start", past is normal.

Yearmonth (YYYYMM)

Accepted: 6-digit integer string, e.g., 202604. Red on: non-6-digit, month < 01 or > 12, year < 1980 or > (current year + 5). Amber on: > 24 months in past (stale series).

Dollar amounts (money)

Accepted: numeric. Parser strips commas, currency symbols, parentheses-for-negative (with negative interpretation), spaces. Decimal precision: 0–2 decimal places. Rejected (red): negative values where column semantics require positive; non-numeric chars beyond the cleanup list. Amber: values > 99th percentile of category-band benchmark (likely data error or genuine outlier — user confirms).

Multi-currency normalization: every money field has an implicit or explicit currency. The loader stores both raw value + raw currency + USD-normalized value using the FX rate as of the load date (sourced from a static FX table refreshed daily; for fictional Lakeshore data, FX rates as of 2026-06-05 are the anchor). Downstream Move calculations use USD-normalized values; reports can render in raw or USD per user preference.

Percent

Accepted: numeric, 0–100 (or 0.0–100.0). Parser strips trailing %. Amber if outside expected band per column semantics (e.g., share_pct in cloud_footprint summing to 100 ± 2pp).

Boolean

Accepted: true, false, True, False, TRUE, FALSE, 1, 0, yes, no, Y, N. Coerced to canonical true/false. Red on any other value.

Enum (controlled vocabulary)

Accepted: exact match against the documented enum list (case-insensitive; coerced to lowercase canonical form). Red on no match. The loader shows a dropdown of valid values in the validation preview to help the user fix.

Email

RFC 5322 syntactic check. Amber if domain is a free-mail provider (gmail.com, yahoo.com, hotmail.com, outlook.com) on a corporate-context column.

Vendor name normalization

Vendor names are the load-bearing cross-HoldCo join key. The loader runs each vendor_name, firm_name, broker_name, carrier_name, provider_name, counterparty_name, external_counsel_firm through the global vendor index. Steps:

  1. Exact match against canonicalized index (e.g., "Microsoft Corporation"). If match: green, use canonical form.
  2. If no exact match, fuzzy match using Levenshtein + token-Jaccard hybrid (threshold 0.85). E.g., "Microsoft Corp" → "Microsoft Corporation" (auto-link with amber). "MSFT" → "Microsoft Corporation" (alias table catches abbreviations).
  3. If still no match, the loader proposes the row's value as a new canonical entry pending the user's confirmation. Confirmed entries are added to the index. Amber until confirmed.

The global vendor index lives at cxo_intel_vendor_index (substrate; see §9). It is shared across all HoldCos within the holding_group so that fuzzy joins on Move 2 cross-HoldCo opportunities resolve correctly. An entry has: canonical_name, aliases[], vendor_type (software, services, audit, insurance, etc.), parent_company (for M&A consolidation — e.g., "Concur" → parent "SAP SE"), cui_url (vendor's homepage, used to disambiguate).

Initial seed of the index includes the top ~500 vendors expected in mid-market PE-style portfolios: all major software (MS, Oracle, SAP, Workday, Salesforce, ServiceNow, NetSuite, etc.), all Big-4 and tier-2 audit/advisory firms, top 50 insurance carriers and brokers, top 30 banks. Seed lives at src/lib/cxo-intel/reference/vendor-seed.json.

Bank name normalization

Same pattern as vendor index but with a curated bank-specific index. Seed includes US top-100 banks plus all G-SIBs internationally. Aliases catch common abbreviations ("JPM", "JPMC", "Chase" all → "JPMorgan Chase"). Bank-name red is rare in practice (banks are well-known); amber appears mostly for small regional/specialty banks not in seed.

Contract renewal date sanity

Composite check across contract_start, contract_end, renewal_notice_days, and "today":

  • contract_end < contract_start → red (impossible)
  • contract_end < today and auto_renew = false → amber (contract expired without renewal?)
  • contract_end - today < renewal_notice_days → amber (renewal action overdue)
  • contract_end > today + 30 years → red (likely typo; e.g., 2207 instead of 2027)

FK integrity

References that span files (e.g., portco_ids in CIO bundle pointing to portco_id in GC entity_registry) are validated at load time and re-validated whenever a related file is loaded later. If the referenced file hasn't been loaded yet, the row is amber with "pending FK resolution"; once the referenced file lands, the loader re-evaluates and either resolves to green or surfaces red on unresolved.

Sum-to-100 invariants

For columns where rows must aggregate to 100% (cloud_footprint.share_pct, it_spend_allocation.share_pct), the validator computes the sum across all rows in the file and checks against 100 ± 2pp. Red on violation; the loader shows the actual sum so the user can identify the rounding/missing-row issue.

Cross-file reconciliation

Some checks span bundles:

  • CFO it_spend_ratios.total_it_spend_usd ≈ sum(CIO it_spend_allocation.annual_usd) within ±15%
  • GC entity_registry.annual_revenue_usd (sum across PortCos under HoldCo) ≈ CFO it_spend_ratios.consolidated_revenue_usd within ±10%
  • CFO insurance_program (cyber line) carrier_name/limit/retention = GC do_eo_cyber_insurance carrier_name/limit/retention
  • CIO vendor_contracts annual_value_usd for HCM vendor = CHRO hcm_stack annual_cost_usd ± 5% (allows for fiscal-year-vs-calendar-year timing)

Cross-file reconciliation runs after every bundle load and surfaces deltas as amber bundle-level flags on the Setup home. Reconciliation doesn't block loads; it surfaces discrepancies for human review.

RLS posture

Every cxo_intel_* data table has two policies:

  1. Tenant-scoped read/write — standard tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id') match, identical to other tenant-scoped tables in the substrate. HoldCo users see their own data fully.
  2. L0 aggregate read — users with role l0_sponsor or l0_op_partner and matching holding_group_id can read rows but only via aggregate views (cxo_intel_agg_*). Transaction-grain reads require explicit grant from the HoldCo's tenant_admin (logged at cxo_intel_grant).

Litigation_pipeline rows with privilege_classification = privileged_attorney_work_product have an additional restriction: only users with role gc, legal_ops, or outside_counsel for the same tenant can read. L0 aggregate read is blocked entirely for those rows.

Upload-event linkage

Every loaded row's upload_id FK resolves to one approval event. When Sentinel generates a sentence like "Morgan Street's Microsoft EA renewal is 2028-06-30 with auto-renew enabled," it cites the source row in cxo_intel_vendor_contracts, which traces through upload_id to "approved by Daniel Okonkwo (CIO) on 2026-06-05 via CSV file vendor_contracts.csv row 3, with co-sign by Sarah Lindqvist (CFO) for > $1M contracts." That citation chain is what makes the "no claim without provenance" rule operational.

Section 10 · Edge cases

Re-upload — full replace vs incremental

The loader supports three re-upload modes; the user picks at step 5 (approval):

ModeSemanticsUse case
full_replaceAll prior rows in the bundle's tables for this tenant are marked superseded_by = new_upload_id and excluded from default reads. New upload's rows are the canonical truth.Annual refresh; CXO recompiles from scratch.
incrementalNew rows are inserted alongside prior rows. Prior rows remain canonical. Conflicts on natural keys (e.g., contract_id, risk_id) supersede the prior row at row-level granularity.Quarterly add-ons; only delta has changed.
partialSame as incremental, but the user explicitly flags that this upload is only a subset of the bundle (e.g., only banking_relationships, not the rest of CFO). System tracks bundle completeness at file level.Wave-by-wave fill-in over multiple sessions.

The default mode for the first upload is full_replace (since there's nothing to supersede). Subsequent loads default to partial with the user opting up to full_replace for an annual refresh. The loader shows a diff preview between current state and incoming upload before approval so the CXO sees exactly what's changing.

Diff preview UX

Wireframe — Diff preview on re-upload
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | CFO bundle / banking_relationships.csv / Diff vs current | | | | Current loaded: 14 rows (uploaded 2026-04-12 by Sarah Lindqvist) | | Incoming: 16 rows (this upload) | | | | Changes: | | [+] 2 new banks: Comerica (operating), Old Natl Bank (operating) | | [~] 3 updated: JPMorgan (annual_fees_usd 460,000 -> 480,000) | | Citi (renewal_date 2026-04-30 -> 2026-09-30) | | Wintrust (h2h_ready false -> true) | | [-] 0 removed | | | | Move impact: | | Move 0 G1 risk grade: P0 -> P0 (still 5 of 16 H2H, ratio 31%) | | Move 0 banking thesis: unchanged (consolidation opportunity preserved) | | | | [ Continue as incremental ] [ Switch to full replace ] [ Cancel ] | +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Multi-currency normalization

Every money field stores three values: raw_value, raw_currency, usd_normalized_value. Normalization uses the FX rate at the row's relevant date (contract_start for contract rows, period_yyyymm for close metric rows, the upload date as default). FX table lives at cxo_intel_fx_rates with daily rates for major currencies. For Lakeshore fictional data, all rows are USD; multi-currency support is required for real customer data (e.g., a HoldCo with European PortCos has EUR-denominated banking and contract data).

Reports default to USD-normalized but a user toggle on any Move surface re-renders in source currency. Cross-HoldCo aggregations always use USD-normalized so the math is consistent.

Vendor name fuzzy match across HoldCos

The cross-HoldCo opportunity surface depends on accurate vendor matching. Morgan Street's "Microsoft Corporation" must join Roosevelt's "Microsoft Corp." must join Lakefront's "MSFT" — all three resolve to canonical "Microsoft Corporation" via the vendor index's alias table.

When a HoldCo loads a new vendor not in the index, the loader proposes it as a candidate canonical entry. If a sibling HoldCo has previously loaded a similar name (fuzzy match across the holding_group's vendor proposals), the loader suggests "this looks similar to 'Concentrix' loaded by Roosevelt on 2026-03-14 — same canonical?" The L0 admin or any HoldCo's admin can confirm the merge.

Merges are tracked at cxo_intel_vendor_merge with the merging user, both source proposals, and the resulting canonical. Sentinel-generated claims about consolidated spend cite both source rows + the merge event.

Same vendor different category across HoldCos

Microsoft sells software (M365, Azure) but also services (Premier Support, Industry Solutions). Two HoldCos might both have "Microsoft Corporation" contracts but in different categories (one in licensing, one in professional_services). The Move 2 consolidation opportunity rolls these together at the parent-vendor level for negotiation leverage but distinguishes the categories in the rationalization view. Loader stores category at the contract row; cross-HoldCo opportunity ranker aggregates by canonical_name and separately by canonical_name + category.

Privileged data handling

Litigation_pipeline rows flagged privileged_attorney_work_product never enter Sentinel general-retrieval embeddings. The loader confirms with the approver: "These N rows are marked attorney-work-product privileged. They will not be indexed for general AI retrieval. Confirm." On confirm, the rows land in the standard table with RLS narrowing reads to GC + outside counsel only and a separate restricted-embedding index used only for GC-scoped queries.

Empty file handling

Some bundles permit empty files (header row only). Examples: GC litigation_pipeline (HoldCo may have no open matters), CIO ai_roadmap (HoldCo may have zero AI activity). The loader accepts an empty file and lands an empty result. The approval flow asks: "You are loading an empty litigation_pipeline.csv. Confirm there are zero open matters at this time?" — explicit attestation prevents accidental empty loads.

Partial bundle blocking

If a downstream Move requires a file that hasn't been loaded, the Move's surface in the app shows: "Blocked — pending CIO ai_roadmap.csv (load via /setup/cxo-intel/cio)." with a deep link. The Setup home shows a per-bundle file checklist with green/grey indicators per file. Tower's "Federated" tab shows L0 view of completeness across all 3 HoldCos.

Re-upload approval propagation

When a row is superseded by a re-upload, prior Sentinel-generated claims that cited that row are flagged as "evidence updated" rather than auto-rewritten. The user (or scheduled refresh job) re-runs the analysis if the underlying data has materially changed. This preserves audit chain — old PDFs/memos that cited the prior row still resolve, but new generation uses the latest.

Load failure recovery

If the substrate write fails mid-transaction (DB unavailable, transient error), the upload event is marked failed in cxo_intel_upload with the error reason. The user sees the failure and a "retry approval" button; the staged CSV files are preserved server-side for 7 days so re-validation isn't required. Approval re-runs the full validation suite (in case data has changed) and writes again. After 7 days, the staged files are purged and the user must re-upload.

Conflicting concurrent loads

Two CXOs (or steward + CXO) attempting to load the same bundle concurrently is rare but possible. The loader uses optimistic concurrency at the bundle-status level: each load attempts to advance the bundle's version number; on conflict, the second loader sees "Sarah Lindqvist (CFO) approved a CFO bundle load 4 minutes ago. Review the load and either resume your draft or discard." This prevents accidental overwrite.

Tenant impersonation by L0 ops

L0 ops users can act on behalf of a HoldCo via the documented impersonation shim. Loader writes include the impersonating user in loaded_by with a flag loaded_via_impersonation = true and the impersonator's identity in impersonator_id. The approval still requires HoldCo CXO sign-off — L0 cannot self-approve a load against a HoldCo's tenant.

Data sovereignty drill-down request

L0 sponsor wants transaction-grain access to a sibling HoldCo's data (e.g., to validate a Move 2 opportunity ranker output). The Tower UI surfaces a "request drill-down" action that emails the target HoldCo's tenant_admin with the rationale; the admin approves or denies in their inbox-style approval queue. Grants are time-bounded (default 30 days) and logged at cxo_intel_grant. Without grant, L0 sees aggregates only.
